subject: Post-discovery: schedule technical deep dive with ML/infra team
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@acme-health.com>, Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@acme-health.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-discovery: schedule technical deep dive with ML/infra team

Hi Anita / Liam —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to hear more about Acme's ingestion pipeline and the latency targets you're aiming for. Quick recap:

- Key goals: reduce inference latency for real-time triage to <200ms P50 for short prompts, and have predictable cost per 1k requests.
- Primary constraints: PHI handling, VPC-only deployment preference, on-prem audit requirements for some hospitals.
- Next step we agreed: a 60–90 minute technical deep dive with your ML + infra engineers so we can map architecture, sizing, and a proposed rollout plan.

Would the team be available for a deep dive next week? Proposed slots (PT):
- Tue 3/21 10:00–11:30
- Wed 3/22 10:00–11:30
- Thu 3/23 14:00–15:30

I've attached the discovery notes and a very rough agenda — easier to iterate once we confirm attendees. Can you confirm who from your ML/infra teams should join (names + roles) and which slot works best?

Draft attendees from our side: myself (AE), Camila (Solutions Eng), Dylan (Infra/ops).

Thanks — looking forward to the deep dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (555) 212-0910
[Attachment: acme-discovery-notes.pdf]

From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@acme-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@acme-health.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-20T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: schedule technical deep dive with ML/infra team

Thanks Marissa — great summary.

Liam (ML lead) and I reviewed the slots; our ML lead + infra engineer can join. Proposed attendees:
- Liam O'Reilly — Head of ML (will lead the model/quality side)
- Rajesh Kumar — Platform Engineer (infra, deployment, networking)

The Wed 3/22 10:00–11:30 PT slot works best for us. Can you confirm a calendar invite and a proposed agenda? Also please include any pre-reads — we'll share a short network diagram ahead of time.

Thanks,
Anita Shah
Director of Product | Acme Health Tech
anita.shah@acme-health.com
[Attaching: acme-network-overview.pdf — will send via Drive link]

Subject: Confirming Wed 3/22 10:00 PT + draft agenda

Anita / Liam —

Great, Wed 3/22 10:00–11:30 PT is confirmed on our side. I just sent a calendar invite (Calendly link: https://calendly.com/marissa/redwood-acme-tech-deep-dive) and attached a short draft agenda.

Draft agenda (60–90 min):
1) Quick intros & goals (5–10m) — align success criteria
2) Acme architecture overview (10–15m) — Liam / Rajesh to present
3) Redwood serving architecture & deployment options (20m) — Camila
   - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
   - Quantization/latency tradeoffs and throughput benchmarking
4) Sizing & cost estimates for expected qps (15m) — Marissa / Camila
5) Integration & network/security (10–15m) — Dylan / Rajesh
6) Next steps & mutual action plan (5–10m)

Attachments: tech-deep-dive-agenda-draft.docx (high level)

Camila / Dylan — can you review and flag any other topics we should add? In particular, can Dylan be ready to cover VPC peering, encryption in transit, and audit log options?

Thanks — will update the invite with the Drive link for pre-reads.

Best,
Marissa
[Attachment: tech-deep-dive-agenda-draft.docx]

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Anita Shah <anita.shah@acme-health.com>, Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@acme-health.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T12:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Confirming Wed 3/22 10:00 PT + draft agenda

Thanks Marissa — agenda looks good. A few suggestions to make the session most productive:

- Ask Acme to share a sample request profile (avg tokens, typical prompt sizes) and a small anonymized dataset for throughput sims.
- I'll prepare:
  * A slide with latency/cost tradeoffs for 8-bit quantization vs bfloat16 (benchmarked on T4/A10x)
  * Recommended batching and caching strategies for low-latency inference
  * Sizing worksheet so we can run rough capacity numbers during the call

- Dylan: can you confirm whether we should ask for VPC peering details ahead of time (CIDR ranges, firewall rules)? That will save time on the call.

I'll attach an architecture overview and a short SE-runbook for run-of-show.

Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
[Attachment: se-architecture-overview.pdf]

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>

All set from infra — I'll join Wed and be prepared to cover:
- VPC peering checklist (CIDR, allowed ports, certs)
- Encryption and key management options (KMS/HSM integrations)
- Audit logs and retention policy options for Private deployment

Quick ask for Acme: if you can share your CIDR and any proxy/load-balancer details ahead of time (Drive link or email), that would be helpful so I can validate the network constraints.

See you Wednesday —
Dylan Brooks
